20-events-and-configuration.html 8/10.

51-contract-terms-and-remedies.html 8/10. A newcomer who knows the basics follows the contract steps well; the main stumbling block is a percentage cap that the practice question uses but the lesson never explains.
51-contract-terms-and-remedies.html 7/10.

50-measures-and-benchmarks.html 8/10, 51-contract-terms-and-remedies.html 7/10. A newcomer would struggle most with the numbers packed into the target-and-benchmark paragraph in lesson 50, and with how a force majeure event changes the daily late amounts in lesson 51, which the lesson describes but never works through.

50-measures-and-benchmarks.html 8/10, 51-contract-terms-and-remedies.html 8/10. A newcomer would most likely stumble on a few plain-looking words used without a clear meaning, such as 'remedies' and 'relief from blame', and on the number 80% doing double duty as both a benchmark and a threshold.

50-measures-and-benchmarks.html 8/10, 51-contract-terms-and-remedies.html 8/10. Both lessons read clearly; a newcomer would mostly stumble over a threshold the first lesson defines but never applies, and over unclear wording about who pays when a contract ends early in the second.

50-measures-and-benchmarks.html 8/10, 51-contract-terms-and-remedies.html 7/10. A newcomer would most struggle with who the contract owner is and which side the project manager is on, since the lessons use that term and the supplier and client roles without saying how they fit together, and with legal words like arbitration that appear without a short meaning.
50-measures-and-benchmarks.html 8/10.

49-balancing-resources.html 8/10. A newcomer would most likely stumble on why the size of a clash decides how far a task can slide, since the lesson gives the float rule without showing the schedule before and after a move.

47-environment-and-assets.html 8/10, 49-balancing-resources.html 8/10. A newcomer would most likely struggle to tell resource leveling from smoothing, and to judge whether a task has enough float to move, because the lesson uses the idea before fully spelling out the limit.

47-environment-and-assets.html 8/10, 48-emotional-intelligence-and-influence.html 7/10. A newcomer would struggle most with the order: a quiz asks about pausing and asking what is behind a reaction before the lesson teaches that, and the four parts of emotional intelligence are not kept clearly apart in the practice items.

47-environment-and-assets.html 9/10, 48-emotional-intelligence-and-influence.html 8/10. Across both lessons, a newcomer would most often stop at a few workplace words used before they are explained, such as sponsor and escalate, and at one awkward quiz question.
